body.estimand_functional: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\) under consistency and event-date transport.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the fixed-design local conditional MSE is at most \(CR_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) without the attainable-direction premise and the local conditional minimax MSE is \(\asymp R_{X,\mathrm{opt}}\) under the disclosed class-richness condition; the accepted anchor estimator has the computable upper certificate \(R_D\).  Marginally, \(\sup_P\operatorname{MSE}_P(\widehat\tau)\le CR_\star\) without the attainable-direction premise, and \(\inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_P\operatorname{MSE}_P(\widetilde\tau)\asymp R_\star\) under the same converse-only condition.

sampling_model.design: For each fixed cohort, \(T\) exact pre-event paths have density bounded above and away from zero.  Conditional analysis uses their optimal-recovery modulus and nearest-site distances; Gram coercivity certifies one estimator but is never a minimax converse.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per calendar window and \(n_s\) treated event outcomes.  Conditional on the full exact design and realized path, untreated responses are centered at \(m_s(X_{st})\), treated outcomes retain their path-conditional mean, and unit histories are independent across units; within-unit temporal and training/event dependence remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path; design-conditional centering does not identify this causal equality.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary, and the random-design density is bounded below there.  Exact fixed-design recovery can nevertheless be much easier than an anchor bandwidth suggests when a site equals the realized path.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event path is generated: deterministic donor folds produce projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains all cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort dependence.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nearest-site and local-constant weights are nonnegative.  The \(\lambda>1\) extension asks when signed higher-order optimal-recovery weights have a uniformly controlled conditional stochastic norm under the existing assumptions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The Gaussian convex-class theory relates minimax estimation of a linear functional to a fixed-design modulus of continuity and near-optimal affine recovery.
Theorems 7 and 8 combine local-polynomial estimation with evaluation at an independent estimated minimizer under strong convexity.
Theorem 1 expands local-linear regression when an estimated covariate is attached to every training observation.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 address replicated classical measurement error on every latent training coordinate by deconvolution.
The ordinary random-design Holder benchmark gives the classical multivariate nonparametric regression rate.
Local-linear smoothers attain ordinary pointwise minimax order under regular fixed or random design.
Ordered moduli characterize finite-sample confidence intervals for linear functionals in known Gaussian experiments.
Bias-aware local-polynomial intervals combine a worst-case bias bound with stochastic calibration.
Synthetic-control prediction intervals account for weight estimation and dependent innovations using block methods.
Proposition 3.1 studies factor-loading recovery when controls and pre-treatment periods jointly grow.

body.tldr: The causal target remains cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a realized event path, identified by consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality.  The repaired observed-law model adds design-conditional centering but leaves within-unit training/event dependence unrestricted.  Fixed-design difficulty is now measured by a joint optimal-recovery modulus for replicated regression means and the full-covariance donor center; the attained dyadic Gram radius is only a computable upper certificate.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), a total nearest-design estimator gives the conditional modulus upper bound without a lower-modulus premise and the matching converse under the disclosed class-richness condition, while the accepted anchor estimator and total concentration interval attain the marginal geometric-mixing rate.  The nonredundant marginal channels are treated replication, calendar spacing, and donor location; the displayed smoothing term is algebraically dominated for fixed cohorts.  Geometric beta mixing incurs \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\), while iid calendars give \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).  Exact constants and the stochastic norm of higher-order signed recovery weights remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine site replication with an externally generated query, while generated-regressor and deconvolution analyses perturb every training coordinate.  The unresolved fixed-design issue is not Gram invertibility but the optimal-recovery modulus of point evaluation under the realized sites and the full donor covariance.
project_justification.niche: Historical market paths may be recorded exactly even when the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors.  This separates a realized-site recovery problem from donor-location uncertainty and from the causal transport assumption.
project_justification.fill: The note derives the causal observed-law functional, defines cohort and joint product-experiment moduli, and proves for rough Holder surfaces a premise-free conditional-risk upper bound and, under the disclosed class-richness condition, a matching frontier equivalent to treated replication, weighted nearest-site spacing, and donor location.  It retains the anchor/extrapolation rule as a computable upper certificate and proves its corrected marginal and honest-length rates.  The common-design-shock construction is excluded by design-conditional centering and is not used as a negative frontier result.

body.related_work: Donoho (1994) supplies the classical Gaussian optimal-recovery link between a linear-functional modulus and near-minimax affine estimation; the present result instead proves a rough-Holder, bounded-response product-experiment comparison with a generated full-covariance query.  Stone (1982) and Fan (1993) give ordinary Holder and pointwise local-polynomial benchmarks but not replicated sites plus a generated center.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) treat generated coordinates attached to every training row, while Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) study classical error in every training coordinate; neither experiment applies here.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) evaluate a sample-split local-polynomial estimator at an estimated minimizer, but strong convexity makes its location error second order.  Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware interval calculations, and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) motivate dependent block calibration.  These sources inform the architecture; the nearest-site characterization, donor-product combination, and three-channel panel frontier are derived in this note.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The no-deconvolution conclusion is conditional on observing every historical path exactly.  The conditional modulus and constructive frontier are proved for \(0<\lambda\le1\), where nearest-site and local-constant response weights are nonnegative and have unit absolute mass.  For \(\lambda>1\), the open extension is to characterize whether higher-order optimal-recovery weights can be selected with conditional stochastic norm uniformly controlled under the existing centering, cross-unit independence, and geometric-mixing assumptions; no new covariance-stability assumption is imposed here.  The geometric-mixing spacing logarithm is retained, with a no-log iid corollary.  Exact phase-intersection constants remain open after centering removes the obsolete common-design-shock witness.
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains an untestable causal restriction.  Design-conditional centering is a separate observed-law sampling condition required for the replicated-response and treated-mean channels; it excludes the former common-design-shock witness but does not determine exact minimax constants.  Upper risk, coverage, and expected-length bounds for \(0<\lambda\le1\) do not require the lower attainable-modulus constant.  The donor and spacing converses use the disclosed sufficient class-richness inequality \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}/256\).  Growing dimension, smoothness adaptation, uniform-in-path bands, exact constants, and higher-order signed-weight stability remain open.
body.interpretation: Conditionally, two exact designs with the same Gram certificate can have different difficulty: a site exactly at the event path removes the spatial recovery component, while a nearby hole leaves a Holder-sized ambiguity.  Marginally, random occupancy converts that ambiguity to the geometric-mixing spacing rate.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds the maximum of treated replication and spacing; otherwise the generated center is asymptotically oracle-negligible.
